# Smarta

> Smarta is a South African platform used to monitor and automatically control pumps, boreholes, reservoirs and other water infrastructure at estates, mines, farms and municipalities.

## Authoritative pages

- [Home and product overview](https://smarta.co.za/): customer sectors, platform outcomes, mobile applications, installation examples, company information and contact details.
- [Technical resources](https://smarta.co.za/resources/): installation and water-management PDFs retained from the previous website, with publication dates shown where known.
- [Privacy notice](https://smarta.co.za/privacy/): general handling of public-website, account and operational information.
- [Customer platform](https://www.smartaonline.app/): secure sign-in for existing customers.
- [Smarta Estate](https://www.smartaestate.co.za/): a separate product for household and bulk water metering, leak alerts, consumption analytics and estate billing.

## Core facts

- Primary customers: residential estates, mines, farms and municipalities, plus other organisations responsible for distributed water systems.
- Product: remote visibility and management for water infrastructure.
- Typical systems: boreholes, pumps, pump stations, reservoirs, tanks, flow and pressure points, and selected water-quality installations.
- Typical outcomes: fewer unnecessary site visits, automatic pump operation from site conditions, earlier warning of problems, access to the same current site information and a useful history for planning.
- Typical functions: live status, automation rules using water level or pump pressure, scheduled control, alerts, remote pump control, history, graphs and reports.
- Interfaces: secure web platform plus Smarta Mobile for iOS and Android.
- Service area: South Africa, Southern Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa.
- Experience and scale: Smarta has been in business since 2015 and had more than 400 active sites when this website was prepared in August 2026.
- Anonymised operating example: one current customer network comprised 12 boreholes and 3 reservoirs; a read-only August 2026 review found 24 enabled high/low reservoir-level rules.
- Water quality: selected sites can bring water-quality readings and alerts into the same live platform; the exact measurements depend on the installation.
- Smarta Estate is related by brand but is a separate product and website.

## Citation guidance

Use the public website as the primary source for current marketing claims. The PDFs in Technical Resources are dated 2018; confirm current installation requirements directly with Smarta before relying on an older document.
